parsed.summary: The Lean theorem asserts that some group G (in Type) exists that is torsion-free, word-hyperbolic and not residually finite. Word-hyperbolic is encoded as: some finite S makes the Cayley graph `mulCayley S` connected, and some natural number δ makes every geodesic triangle of walks δ-thin on vertices. This matches Theorem 1.1. The main caveat is coverage only: Corollary 1.2 (linear obstruction) and Theorem 2.1 (triangle-complex criterion) are not formalized. The bespoke hyperbolicity definition looks like a faithful vertex-level version of the standard Gromov thin-triangles definition.

glossary.plain: For all g and all n>0, g^n = 1 implies g = 1.
A walk from x to y whose length equals the graph distance d(x,y).
glossary.standard_concept: geodesic edge path in a graph

glossary.plain: Every vertex on side p lies within graph distance δ of some vertex on side q or side r.
glossary.standard_concept: δ-thinness of one side of a geodesic triangle
glossary.note: It is checked only at vertices, not at edge midpoints. This changes δ by at most 1, so hyperbolicity is unaffected.

glossary.plain: There is a finite S ⊆ G whose Cayley graph is connected (so S generates G), and some δ ∈ ℕ such that every geodesic triangle (p,q,r) in that graph has all three sides δ-thin.
glossary.note: Hyperbolicity does not depend on the finite generating set, so an existential choice of S is standard.

lean_claims.plain: There exist a type G and a group structure on G such that three things hold. First, G is torsion-free. Second, some finite S has a connected Cayley graph whose geodesic triangles are uniformly δ-thin. Third, G is not residually finite in Mathlib's sense (Group.ResiduallyFinite).

paper_claims.plain: There exists a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite.
For this G, every field K, every n ≥ 1 and every homomorphism ρ: G → GL_n(K), the finite residual R_f(G) is contained in ker ρ. In particular G is not linear over any field.

Let K be a finite Euclidean triangle complex with a link condition (every cyclically reduced closed link walk has angular length ≥ 2π+η). Then π1(K) is torsion-free and hyperbolic, and paths whose turns are all at least π are not nullhomotopic.

coverage.why: All three properties are encoded with standard meanings.
There is no statement about linear representations.
This is an intermediate criterion and is not stated in Lean.

flags.explanation: Only the headline existence theorem is formalized. The linear-obstruction corollary and the triangle-complex criterion are absent.

Thinness is required only at vertices of the Cayley graph, using graph distance and geodesic walks. Points interior to edges are ignored, which is standard up to a shift δ ↦ δ+1. Faithfulness also relies on `SimpleGraph.mulCayley` having the usual Cayley-graph adjacency (left or right multiplication by elements of S, symmetrized).
flags.probe_idea: Check the definition of SimpleGraph.mulCayley: prove `(SimpleGraph.mulCayley S).Adj a b ↔ a ≠ b ∧ ∃ s ∈ S, a * s = b ∨ b * s = a` (or the left-multiplication analogue).
